rules: Standalone signals: no case, entity or map-line links. Incident date kept apart from report date; for an arrest the pin date is the arrest and older alleged conduct is given in words, not as the pin date. Priority Intelligence: no one is named; the accused are described as accused, charges are given as charged, allegations (including any claimed syndicate or network) are attributed and the case status is stated; no sexual-offence cases. Killings: private individuals (victims and suspects) are not named; where a party to the shooting (police or soldiers) gives the only account, the pin says so and that account is attributed, not adopted. One police precinct per area: the Neltox pin is in the Tshamutumbu precinct and is not merged into Musina. Being near another pin is not a link. Estimated map points: the title says 'map point estimated' and the drawer location note starts 'ESTIMATED MAP POINT'. Every fact-base quote matched word for word against the saved source text.

signals.title: Matswale Phase 12, Musina (map point estimated): liquor store owner, 37, shot dead in his store; no arrest, 16 Oct
signals.content: Police say a 37-year-old businessman was shot dead inside his liquor store at Matswale Phase 12, Musina, at about 20:00 on Friday 16 October. His wife, who was at the scene, told police he was preparing to close when an unknown man came in, handed him a R200 note and asked to buy liquor, then allegedly opened fire while he fetched it from the fridge. He had more than 20 gunshot wounds to the upper body and was declared dead at the scene; about 23 spent cartridges were found (police spokesperson Capt Vuledzani Dathi, via Limpopo Mirror). Musina police opened a murder case. Police say the motive and the suspect's identity are unknown; no arrest has been reported. The victim is not named here. One public report, resting on police: Limpopo Mirror, 22 October. The map point is estimated: Matswale Phase 12 could not be placed on a map, so the pin is a Musina township reference point, not the store.

signals.title: Neltox, Tshamutumbu police area (map point estimated): man shot dead after exchange of fire with SANDF patrol; police investigating, 11 Oct
signals.content: An unidentified man was found shot dead in the bushes in the Neltox area, in the Tshamutumbu policing area near the Zimbabwe border, at about 10:30 on Sunday 11 October; Tshamutumbu police are investigating (Vhembe SAPS spokesperson Capt Vuledzani Dathi, via Limpopo Mirror). According to police, SANDF members on patrol tried to stop a white Toyota Fortuner; the occupants drove off at high speed, then jumped out when they realised the soldiers were pursuing them and allegedly opened fire on the soldiers, who returned fire. One of them was later found in the bushes with bullet wounds and declared dead. Soldiers are a party to this shooting, and the only account of it is the one police relay; no independent account and no finding on who fired first or who fired the fatal shot has been reported. The man has not been identified. One public report: Limpopo Mirror, 15 October. The map point is estimated: Neltox could not be placed on a map, so the pin is the Tshamutumbu police station point, a reference only.

signals.title: Musina (map point estimated): one arrested over R1.5m in illicit cigarettes; police allege a syndicate, leader at large, 19 Oct
signals.content: A man was arrested on Monday 19 October during an intelligence-led police operation at premises in Musina suspected of being used to store large quantities of illicit cigarettes (Limpopo police spokesperson Col Malesela Ledwaba, via Limpopo Mirror, 21 October). Police say they recovered 55 boxes and 46 cartons of Remington Gold cigarettes valued at about R1.5 million, and seized two vehicles worth about R600,000 together. He faces charges of possession and transportation of illicit cigarettes and was expected to appear in the Musina Magistrate's Court on 21 October; the outcome of that appearance is not reported in the saved source. Police describe the target as an alleged illicit cigarette syndicate and say the suspected syndicate leader and four others fled and are being traced. The syndicate is a police allegation; no court has found one, no one has been convicted, and the accused is not named here. Case status: charged; court outcome not reported. One report, resting on a police statement. The map point is estimated: the premises are not identified, so the pin is the Musina police station point, a reference within the town.

signals.title: Beitbridge border post (approx.): North West businessman charged 21 Oct as co-accused over two Absa-financed cars intercepted in Jul
signals.content: A North West businessman was charged on 21 October and first appeared in the Musina Magistrate's Court on 22 October, added as a co-accused in a case over two vehicles intercepted at the Beitbridge border post on 22 July (Limpopo Mirror and Review Online, 22 October). According to police and the NPA, police at the border post intercepted two vehicles, still financed by Absa, that were allegedly being taken from Mahikeng to Malawi; lawful bank authorisation to move them across the border was allegedly not obtained and fraudulent bank documents were allegedly arranged instead. Two people were arrested in July and remain in custody, due in the Musina Regional Court on 27 October; the vehicles were handed back to Absa. The NPA alleges the businessman acted in collusion with his employees. The reported charges differ: Limpopo Mirror lists attempted theft and fraud, Review Online attempted theft and money laundering. These are allegations: no one has been convicted, and the accused are not named here. Case status: charged and appeared in court; the reports do not give a consistent next date for his case, so none is stated here. Two outlets, both resting on police and NPA statements. The pin marks the South African border control at Beitbridge, where the July interception happened; the October charge and court appearance were not at this point, and the July date is the alleged conduct, not the pin date.
